title: Chicken and Leek Pie
subtitle: Poached chicken and slow-cooked leeks in a light cream sauce
excerpt: Chicken and leek pie is a lighter, more delicately flavoured pie than the mushroom version. The leeks soften down to almost a purée in places, giving the sauce a natural sweetness. It is a spring and autumn pie, pale and gentle, with tarragon or parsley finishing the filling.
sourceNotes: British white-sauce pie tradition. Welsh-inspired variant using leek as the primary vegetable, with influence from Scottish and Welsh home-cooking traditions where leek features prominently in poultry dishes.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the unbaked assembled pie for up to 2 months. Bake from frozen at 180°C for 50 to 55 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling up to 2 days ahead. Cool and refrigerate. Assemble and bake just before serving.

content.text: Chicken and leek pie is the more delicate British pie: poached chicken in a cream sauce built on the poaching stock, with leeks cooked until very soft and sweet. The flavour is gentler than the mushroom version and the colour is pale. It suits spring and autumn when leeks are at their best, and it is the kind of pie that children tend to accept without complaint.

items.prepNote: white and pale green parts, thinly sliced

content.text: Poach the chicken and make the sauce

Place the chicken thighs in a saucepan, cover with cold water, and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 18 to 20 minutes until just cooked through. Lift out and reserve 400 ml of the poaching liquid, strained. When cool enough to handle, shred the chicken into large pieces.

Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the leeks and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until very soft and sweet but not coloured. Sprinkle over the flour, stir to coat, and cook for 1 minute.

Gradually add the reserved chicken stock, stirring constantly. Add the double cream and the mustard if using. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until thickened. Fold in the chicken and parsley. Taste and season well. Tip into the pie dish and cool completely.

Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Lay the pastry over the cooled filling, pressing the edges to the rim. Trim, crimp, and cut two small vents. Brush with beaten egg. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until puffed and golden.

items.symptom: Leeks are watery inside the finished pie
items.cause: The leeks were not cooked long enough before the sauce was built
items.fix: Cook the leeks until properly soft and the moisture has mostly evaporated: at least 12 minutes over medium-low heat. Watery leeks dilute the sauce from within.

items.symptom: Sauce is too thick and pasty
items.cause: Too much flour relative to liquid
items.fix: Loosen with a splash more chicken stock before folding in the chicken. The sauce should be thick but still pour slowly from a spoon.

items.cause: The oven was not hot enough or the pie was placed on too high a shelf
items.fix: Use the lower middle rack so the base pastry gets heat from below. For a double-crust version, blind bake the base for 15 minutes before filling.

items.cause: The poaching liquid was unseasoned and the sauce lacked salt
items.fix: Season the poaching water with a teaspoon of salt. Taste the sauce critically before assembly: it should be well seasoned.

content.text: Chicken and leek is a classic pairing in British and Celtic cooking. It appears in Welsh cawl and cock-a-leekie broth. The pie version is home-kitchen food rather than restaurant food. It is mild and creamy, and it tends to be a recipe that gets made for the whole family.
